# CQ-HECS: Classical Quantum High-Efficiency Compute Simulator & Four-Path Engine

> Deterministic classical quantum emulator & ARX constraint solver with Z[1/sqrt(2), i] exact ring arithmetic, Vulkan 1.3 compute backend, and Four-Path architecture.

CQ-HECS (Classical Quantum High-Efficiency Compute Simulator) is a high-performance compute engine and constraint solver written in C++20 and Vulkan 1.3 with cross-vendor SPIR-V compute shaders (AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, Apple/MoltenVK).

## Core Capabilities & Architectural Axioms

- **Cross-Vendor Vulkan 1.3 Compute Backend**: Hardware-agnostic SPIR-V compute shaders for tensor contraction and exact ring arithmetic without proprietary CUDA lock-in.
- **Exact Giles-Selinger Ring Arithmetic Z[1/sqrt(2), i]**: Bit-exact algebraic tracking without floating-point rounding drift. Complete Clifford+T gate set representation ($U^\dagger U = I$).
- **Scientific Entanglement Scaling**: Memory-efficient MPS for Area-Law states (GHZ, 1D lattices); transparent fallback to Path D (Sparse-Pauli with proven error bound) or unresolved state for Volume-Law states.
- **ARX Carry-Shadow Separation**: Linearizes modular addition via carry-shadow splitting for symmetric cryptanalysis verification (ChaCha20: 20 rounds, SHA-256: 64 rounds, BLAKE2b: 12 rounds) as an algebraic verification testbench.
- **DIMACS CNF SAT Solving**: DPLL search with an O(1) Hilbert-Cuckoo cycle loop pruner running Murmur3 state signatures.
- **Vulkan Workload & Entropy Scheduler**: Dynamic queue submission, memory barriers, and heuristic routing stabilized by hardware entropy harvested from OS timer jitter.
- **Zero Runtime Dependencies**: Monolithic executable (`cq_hecs.exe`) and pure C-ABI shared library (`cq_hecs.dll`). Shaders are embedded as static C++ byte arrays.
